 Télétravail / mode hybride
 Les candidatures peuvent être prises en considération partout dans le pays d’emploi. Toutefois, les personnes qui se trouvent à moins de 80 km du Markham Elevation Centre devront travailler sur place trois jours par semaine.
 
 Description du poste
 General Motors est un chef de file mondial dans le domaine des systèmes avancés d’aide à la conduite. Grâce à la technologie mains libres Super Cruise, présente dans plus de 500 000 véhicules équipés de Super Cruise en circulation et ayant parcouru plus de 700 millions de kilomètres en mode mains libres, GM démontre que l’automatisation peut être fiable, intuitive et utile. GM possède la portée mondiale nécessaire pour offrir à grande échelle des avancées de pointe aux conducteurs de tous les jours. Joignez-vous à nous pour contribuer à la prochaine génération d’expériences personnelles de conduite autonome, sécuritaires et agréables.
 
 À propos de l’organisation
 L’équipe Évaluation développe et fait évoluer l’écosystème d’évaluation qui soutient le développement et la mise à l’échelle des technologies de conduite autonome de GM. Nous développons des indicateurs, des flux de travail automatisés et des approches analytiques qui permettent de prendre des décisions fondées sur les données dans l’ensemble du développement et de la vérification des systèmes de conduite autonome. En collaboration avec les équipes de l’autonomie, de la simulation, des systèmes et de la sécurité, nous agissons comme intégrateurs au niveau du système et arbitres de la qualité de bout en bout des systèmes de conduite autonome. Nous sommes responsables de vastes bibliothèques de scénarios de test, de pipelines d’évaluation continue ainsi que de composants essentiels liés à l’évaluation des risques et aux critères de mise en production. Nous considérons les essais routiers, l’exploration de données, l’entraînement et les indicateurs comme des cas d’utilisation de premier ordre au sein d’un cadre analytique unifié. En vous joignant à cette équipe, vous contribuerez à façonner les plateformes d’évaluation fondamentales de GM, à transformer les résultats au niveau du système en rétroaction claire et à accélérer le déploiement validé de systèmes de conduite autonome à grande échelle.
 Responsabilités
 Définir la stratégie et l’architecture des indicateurs et des analyses servant à évaluer la performance des logiciels de conduite autonome dans l’ensemble de la pile technologique d’autonomie.

 Diriger des initiatives interfonctionnelles avec les équipes de l’autonomie, de l’ingénierie des systèmes, de la simulation et des données afin d’intégrer l’évaluation aux flux de développement et aux décisions de mise en production.

 Concevoir et piloter de nouvelles méthodes statistiques et d’apprentissage automatique, ainsi que des techniques d’introspection des modèles d’apprentissage automatique, afin de quantifier la performance, de détecter les régressions et de révéler les tendances du comportement des systèmes à grande échelle.

 Assurer la responsabilité des principaux indicateurs et KPI d’évaluation des systèmes de conduite autonome utilisés pour prendre des décisions relatives à l’état de préparation et à la sécurité; synthétiser et présenter les résultats ainsi que les compromis aux parties prenantes; rendre les informations facilement accessibles aux équipes partenaires au moyen de tableaux de bord interactifs.

 Compétences et aptitudes requises
 Au moins 7 ans d’expérience pratique dans le développement de logiciels pour la robotique ou les systèmes autonomes, couvrant plusieurs sous-systèmes, de la perception à la planification et au contrôle du véhicule.

 Au moins 3 ans d’expérience à diriger l’évaluation de systèmes dynamiques complexes au moyen d’approches numériques et d’apprentissage automatique appliquées à de grandes quantités de données de séries temporelles.

 Maîtrise du développement Python dans des environnements de production en équipe; grande capacité à travailler dans de vastes bases de code C++ liées à l’autonomie.

 Expérience démontrée en leadership technique interfonctionnel, notamment dans la définition de stratégies adoptées par plusieurs équipes et l’influence exercée sur les décisions relatives aux systèmes et à l’architecture.

 Diplôme de doctorat, de maîtrise ou de baccalauréat en informatique, robotique, génie mécanique ou aérospatial, apprentissage automatique ou dans un domaine connexe.

 Atouts
 Expérience en conduite autonome ou en robotique de terrain à enjeux élevés; expérience de la conception, de l’exécution et de l’interprétation d’expériences de simulation et d’essais sur le terrain à grande échelle.

 Connaissance approfondie de la modélisation statistique, de la conception expérimentale et des tests d’hypothèses appliqués à l’évaluation des systèmes autonomes; maîtrise de Pandas, NumPy, SciPy et des bibliothèques de visualisation.

 Maîtrise de C++ et de SQL, ainsi qu’expérience dans la définition de la journalisation, des schémas de données et des pipelines d’évaluation pour les essais de systèmes autonomes à grande échelle.

 Expérience avec ROS ou d’autres mécanismes de communication interprocessus, la journalisation des piles technologiques robotiques et les bases de données d’expériences à grande échelle, y compris la conception ou la mise à l’échelle de plateformes d’évaluation.

 Expérience en modélisation des interactions entre agents et en définition ou en gestion de critères et de processus de décision pour la mise en production de systèmes autonomes.

Job Description 
 Role Overview
 As a Senior Software Engineer on the Rendering Infrastructure team, you will build the systems that turn a GPU-accelerated, physically-based sensor simulator into a production platform — one that runs reproducibly, at cluster scale, and against production-representative autonomous vehicle interfaces. This is a systems role at the boundary of rendering, simulation, perception, and distributed infrastructure. You will connect the renderer to AV software stacks and compute clusters, reproduce real sensor scheduling and vehicle timing, run many worlds concurrently on a single GPU, and make the runtime start fast and stay cheap across thousands of workers. Your work determines whether closed-loop simulation — the vehicle software in the loop with the renderer, not just offline synthetic data generation — is trustworthy and affordable: whether a run reproduces, whether synthetic sensor feeds arrive with the same timing quirks the real vehicle sees, and how many scenarios we can execute per GPU-hour. We build in modern C++ and Python on Linux, with ROS, PyTorch, CUDA, NVIDIA OptiX, NVIDIA MDL, and OpenUSD. We're looking for someone who enjoys this layer — debugging nondeterminism across a process boundary, cutting cold-start time by changing how a runtime is packaged, and reasoning about GPU memory and IPC in the same conversation.
 
 About the Team
 The Rendering Infrastructure team owns the foundational systems the broader Rendering team builds on top of: asset and scene ingestion, GPU memory and resource management, acceleration structure construction, packaging and deployment, profiling infrastructure, and the core engine abstractions of our physically-based sensor simulation system. We also own how the renderer connects to the AV stack and world simulator, as a library or a service, and how consumers configure it — what it produces, at what fidelity, and how it behaves when something goes wrong. We sit between the rendering algorithms team and everyone who consumes simulated sensor data — perception training, closed-loop validation and reinforcement learning. We care about determinism, throughput per GPU, iteration speed, and infrastructure that stays comprehensible as it scales.
 
 Why Join Us?
 Work on hard systems problems with an unusually clear definition of success — reproducibility, timing fidelity, frames per second per GPU, and worker spin-up time are all measurable, and all of them matter. Own meaningful surface area: the AV stack integration and transport layer, the sensor scheduling and timing model, multi-world rendering on a single GPU, or the runtime deployment and asset delivery path, depending on your strengths. Sit at the center of the simulation stack, where rendering, perception, and infrastructure meet, and see your work used across the organization for perception training, closed-loop simulation, and reinforcement learning. Join a team that pairs rigor — design documents, reproducibility, profiling, and regression testing — with pragmatic engineering and short feedback loops.
 
 What You'll Do
 You will own one or more of the following areas and contribute across the others, depending on your strengths and team priorities.
 Connect the renderer to AV software stacks and compute clusters — designing low-latency, high-bandwidth transport using ROS/ROS 2, shared-memory IPC, gRPC, and sockets with appropriate serialization formats, and streaming multi-sensor payloads into the autonomous vehicle stack.
 Integrate the renderer with learned driving models through Gymnasium-style environment APIs — stepping the simulation from Python, exchanging observations and actions efficiently with PyTorch-based models, and preserving deterministic execution while minimizing per-step overhead for eval and training at scale.
 Integrate the runtime with the cloud and on-premises execution environments used for large-scale closed-loop testing, continuous integration, and perception training pipelines.
 Improve and validate deterministic execution — establishing the required bit-accurate or frame-deterministic lock-step behavior across the simulation clock, dynamic physics updates, and the ray-traced renderer, and building the tooling that demonstrates a run reproduces to the agreed bar.
 Reproduce real sensor scheduling and vehicle timing — staggered camera exposures, rolling shutter behavior, LiDAR spin and packet rates, hardware clock drift, and the onboard constraints perception actually operates under, including P95/P99 compute latency, transport lag, and packet drops.
 Build perturbation mechanisms that inject timing jitter, dropped or out-of-order frames, and calibration drift in both extrinsics and intrinsics, and use them to stress-test downstream perception and sensor fusion robustness in closed-loop runs.
 Build memory-efficient multi-world and multi-scenario execution inside a single rendering process, using shared geometry and instancing — OptiX IAS/GAS, or the analogous acceleration structure hierarchies in Vulkan/DXR — so concurrent rollouts share static map geometry instead of duplicating it in GPU memory.
 Optimize GPU memory footprint, scene streaming, and execution scheduling to maximize frames per second per GPU across concurrent simulation workers.
 Improve runtime deployment and asset delivery — deterministic deployment packages (SquashFS archives, read-only container layers, memory-mapped storage) and low-overhead loaders for OpenUSD scene graphs and NVIDIA MDL materials that work against compressed, read-only filesystems without redundant decompression or copies.
 Build distributed caches for textures, precompiled OptiX/PTX shader pipelines, and prebuilt acceleration structures to eliminate cold-start compilation and redundant I/O at cluster scale.
 Profile and reduce disk, network, and memory footprints to cut worker spin-up time, binary payload size, and asset ingestion overhead.
 Partner with the 3D content and USD pipeline teams to set runtime budgets, automated validation rules, and compression workflows before assets enter deployment.
 Uphold high standards through technical design documents, code review, reproducibility and performance regression testing, and mentorship of other engineers.
 
 What You Must Have
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a substantial portion focused on performance-critical systems software.
 Production proficiency in modern C++ (C++17/20), including performance optimization, memory management, and clean API and system design in a large codebase, plus working proficiency in Python for tooling and automation.
 Strong Linux systems programming foundation: multithreading and concurrency, memory management, IPC, and high-throughput data movement, including systems that operate across process and machine boundaries.
 Depth in at least one of the two domains this role bridges, and the interest to grow into the other: Robotics or autonomous systems — the architecture and integration of perception, planning, or control components, and experience with at least one interface those systems are driven through: real-time middleware (ROS/ROS 2, DDS, custom IPC, or high-rate publish/subscribe) and / or a Gymnasium-style environment API; or

GPU programming through a compute or ray tracing API (CUDA, OptiX, Vulkan, DXR, or similar), with a working understanding of GPU memory and execution models.
 
 A track record of designing, implementing, and debugging reliable distributed systems, including the nondeterminism and failure modes that come with them.
 Experience profiling and optimizing real systems, and the instinct to measure before optimizing.
 Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work across rendering, simulation, perception, infrastructure, and content pipeline teams.
 
 Bonus Points
 Experience in one or more of the following is helpful; we do not expect any candidate to have all of it.
 Working knowledge of how autonomous driving perception stacks ingest sensor feeds — sensor scheduling, staggered exposures, rolling shutter, LiDAR packet rates, and onboard compute and transport latency budgets.
 Experience designing closed-loop simulation edge cases and perturbations: schedule jitter, dropped frames, out-of-order packets, and calibration or extrinsics drift.
 Experience with batched rendering, multi-viewport rendering, or multi-scenario execution on a single GPU using acceleration structure hierarchies and instancing (OptiX IAS/GAS, Vulkan/DXR TLAS/BLAS).
 Strength in both domains above rather than one — GPU systems, and robotics or autonomous systems — or practical depth in ray tracing and path tracing specifically (NVIDIA OptiX, Vulkan Ray Tracing, or DirectX Raytracing). 

Hands-on Linux deployment optimization: SquashFS, loop devices, memory-mapped files, zero-copy loading, container overlay layers, and cold-start reduction across compute nodes.
 Experience designing high-performance texture and shader caching systems — OptiX disk cache, Vulkan pipeline cache, or PTX distribution.
 Experience consuming OpenUSD in a C++ runtime and optimizing stage traversal and runtime memory layout.
 Familiarity with deploying and scaling containerized simulation jobs on cloud platforms (AWS, GCP) or on-premises HPC clusters.
 Exposure to autonomous vehicle or robotics simulation platforms such as NVIDIA Omniverse, Isaac Sim, DRIVE Sim, Unreal Engine, or custom in-house simulators.
 Experience supporting reinforcement learning environments or Gymnasium-style simulation interfaces as downstream consumers.
 Evidence of technical contribution through open-source rendering, simulation, or systems infrastructure work, internal platforms, publications, or other knowledge sharing.
 
 Candidate Profile
 Relevant experience may come from robotics, perception, simulation, rendering and graphics, game engines, HPC, or distributed systems infrastructure. Direct autonomous vehicle experience is not required. Successful candidates will combine strong software engineering fundamentals with practical intuition for sensor data, simulation timing, GPU execution, and distributed runtime environments.
 
 Compensation
 The compensation information is a good faith estimate only. It is based on what a successful applicant might be paid in accordance with applicable state laws. The compensation may not be representative for positions located outside of New York, Colorado, California, or Washington.
 The salary range for this role is $153,200 to $234,100. The actual base salary a successful candidate will be offered within this range will vary based on factors relevant to the position.
 Bonus Potential: An incentive pay program offers payouts based on company performance, job level, and individual performance.
 
 Benefits
 GM offers a variety of health and wellbeing benefit programs. Benefit options include medical, dental, vision, Health Savings Account, Flexible Spending Accounts, retirement savings plan, sickness and accident benefits, life insurance, paid vacation & holidays, tuition assistance programs, employee assistance program, GM vehicle discounts and more.
 
 Hybrid/Remote
 This role can be based remotely.

jobs.description:
Job Description 
 
 At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.   
 
 Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale. 
 
 The Role 
 The advancement of virtual tools has improved the way hardware and software can be optimized in vehicle design. As a Senior Virtual Hardware Model Engineer, you have the unique opportunity to shape GM's future by partnering cross functionally to develop models that unlock our ability to optimize design parameters within hardware components. In this role, you will lead development of select models in collaboration with suppliers, product development engineers, and other systems, software, and virtual teams.
 
 What You’ll Do (Responsibilities) 
 Develop high-fidelity component plant models in MATLAB/Simulink that mathematically emulate the electrical, mechanical/physics, and software interfaces of GVHE hardware components.

 Collaborate cross-functionally (Tech Specialists, DREs, VDDV, SIL, CoSim, suppliers) to understand hardware designs, control strategies, and boundary conditions, and translate them into clear modeling requirements.

 Implement plant models in a form suitable for use in GM CoSim environments (e.g., FMU export), ensuring correct I/O definitions, signal naming, and execution behavior.

 Use supplier specifications, design data, and physical test/bench/vehicle results to parameterize, correlate, and continuously improve model fidelity.

 Support integration of component plant models into larger system and vehicle-level co-simulation environments, working closely with simulation integration and CoSim architecture teams.

 Leverage plant models as virtual harness/component testers to confirm performance, run what-if studies, and explore fault and edge-case behavior before hardware is available.

 Document modeling assumptions, limitations, calibration parameters, and validation results to enable reuse and traceability across programs.

 Lead development and maintenance of model requirements documentation (Appendix C11, C12), with technical leadership in developing component plant model requirements, test needs, and deliverables are clearly specified and up to date.

 Contribute to standard methods, libraries, and best practices for component plant modeling within GVHE, mentoring peers and helping scale the capability across programs

 Own system-level modeling strategy across multiple components/domains (e.g., closures, thermal, chassis), including how component plant models roll up into integration/system models.

 Define and drive standards and best practices for model architecture, naming, fidelity levels, correlation methods, and validation criteria across programs.

 Lead model correlation and validation strategy: decide which tests/data are needed, set acceptance thresholds, and arbitrate trade-offs between fidelity and runtime.

Your Skills and Abilities (Required Qualifications) 
 Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Math, Physics, Computer Science, or other relevant degree

 Minimum 5 years of experience in product development, systems engineering, or work related to software/hardware connectivity. Preferred experience in translating physical phenomena into mathematical/Simulink models (electrical, mechanical, and software I/O).

 Proficiency with Matlab/Simulink or similar software that uses code-based logic for model-based simulation.

 Track record of delivering complex multi-domain models (coupled electrical–mechanical–software behavior) into SIL/HIL/CoSim workflows.

 Strong communication and collaboration skills

 Skilled and proficient with a variety of field’s concepts, practices, and procedures.

 Extensive personal experience and discernment to plan and accomplish goals.

 Ability to perform multiple tasks. Lead and likely direct the work of others. A wide degree of creativity and latitude is expected .

Job Description 
 The Role 
 The Safety Assurance for Effective Autonomous Driving Software (SAFE-ADS) department is part of GM’s Global Product Safety, System, and Certification (GPSSC) organization. SAFE-ADS brings together technical and operational expertise to help ensure the safe development, testing, launch, and continuous improvement of automated driving systems (ADS).   

 GM is seeking an   Autonomous Vehicle Safety Assurance Technical Program Manager   to lead integrated execution across the SAFE-ADS operating plan. 
 
 This staff individual contributor will bring structure, momentum, and transparency to technically complex workstreams spanning safety risk management, operational safety, human factors, software validation, safety metrics, rules-of-the-road compliance, counterfactual simulation, and related system-safety interfaces.   

The successful candidate will connect strategy to delivery by translating operating-plan objectives into actionable roadmaps, aligning cross-functional teams to milestones and measurable outcomes, managing technical dependencies and risks, and driving decisions to closure across engineering, validation, data, operations, legal, public policy, and product organizations.   

This role is ideal for an experienced technical program leader who can   operate   at both the systems level and in execution details, communicate effectively with technical and executive audiences, and improve the processes and tools used to deliver safety-critical software and assurance programs.   

What   You’ll   Do   

 Program Execution   

 Own the integrated execution model for SAFE-ADS operating-plan initiatives, including   objectives , milestones, dependencies, resources, risks, decisions, and deliverables.   

Translate product requirements, program milestones, and   operating -plan commitments into clear workstream charters, roadmaps, delivery plans, and ownership models.   

Coordinate planning-cycle updates and ensure changes to   scope,   priorities, dependencies, and capacity are reflected across relevant plans.   

Establish governance, status reporting, action tracking, decision logs, escalation paths, and program reviews that keep execution visible and predictable.   

Drive risk mitigation and recovery plans, escalating technical, schedule, resource, and dependency issues with decision-ready recommendations.   

Partner with engineering, operations, quality, Legal, and GPSSC stakeholders on incident response, investigations, corrective actions, retrospectives, and continuous improvement.   

Improve workflows, dashboards, automations, and data quality across Jira, Jira Align,   Confluence,     SharePoint , requirements tools, and related systems.   

Safety Assurance   

Manage dependencies among human-factors studies, operational data, safety requirements, validation criteria, readiness assessments, and program milestones.   

Lead cross-functional execution for aggregate safety metrics and rules-of-the-road initiatives, including metric definitions, data quality, benchmarking, targets, validation, dashboards, and monitoring.   

Coordinate interfaces with functional safety, SOTIF, ADAS and AV system safety, architecture, sensing and integration, software validation, simulation, data engineering, platform, and vehicle-integration teams.   

Ensure requirements, assumptions, design changes, validation activities, and readiness decisions are visible across workstreams and linked to program outcomes.   

Translate technical trade-offs and   impact   assessments into clear program decisions, actions, risks, and leadership communications.   

Coordinate the supporting work needed to keep assurance deliverables, evidence plans, assessments, and readiness decisions aligned with program milestones.   

Facilitate alignment among safety   objectives , claims, sufficiency criteria, requirements, test plans, evidence owners, assessment activities, and documented decisions.   

Maintain traceability across requirements, work items, tests, metrics, evidence, risks, changes, and approvals using   appropriate systems   and   tools.

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, systems engineering, robotics, safety engineering, mathematics, or   a related   technical field.   

7+ years of relevant experience leading complex technical programs in autonomous vehicles, ADAS, software-intensive systems, systems engineering, product safety, safety assurance, or another safety-critical domain.   

At least 3 years of experience in technical program management, engineering program management, software delivery, systems engineering leadership, or an equivalent role with responsibility for execution across multiple technical teams.   

Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional programs with multiple workstreams, stakeholders, dependencies, and enterprise-level visibility.   

Strong program management capabilities, including integrated planning, roadmap and milestone management, dependency tracking, risk and issue management, governance, change control, resource planning, and executive communication.   

Experience translating ambiguous technical   objectives   into structured execution plans, measurable outcomes, clear ownership, and decision-ready reporting.   

Experience working with software development lifecycles, software validation, test and verification activities, release planning, CI/CD or equivalent engineering workflows, and production-readiness practices.   

Working knowledge of requirements management, end-to-end traceability, configuration management, impact analysis, evidence management, and assessment processes.   

Hands-on experience with Jira and familiarity with Jira Align, Confluence, SharePoint, Smartsheet, or comparable   program-management   and collaboration tools.   

Experience using or administering requirements and traceability tools such as IBM DOORS Next Generation (DNG), Jama Connect, or equivalent systems.   

Familiarity with metrics, dashboards, data-quality practices, and reporting workflows used to measure program health and technical readiness.   

Ability to understand and connect technical work across software, AI/ML, systems engineering, validation, simulation, human factors, operations, and product safety.   

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor information for technical, operational, and executive audiences.   

Ability to influence without authority, build alignment across functions, work through ambiguity, and drive action to closure.   

Passion for autonomous vehicle technology and safe deployment of advanced driving capabilities.   

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications) 

Project Management Professional (PMP), Program Management Professional ( PgMP ), PMI Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP ),     Scrum , or another recognized program/project management certification.   

Experience with Jira Align portfolio planning .   

Experience with IBM DOORS Next Generation, Jama Connect, requirements databases, test-management systems, or safety-case and evidence-management platforms.   

Experience with autonomous vehicle or ADAS safety assurance, safety management systems, safety issue management, operational safety, human factors, or product launch readiness.   

Familiarity with functional safety, SOTIF, AI/ML safety, rules-of-the-road compliance, safety performance metrics, or safety-critical software development.   

Familiarity with Goal Structuring Notation (GSN) or another structured argumentation framework.   

Experience with Agile at scale, program increments, release trains, phase-gate development, or hybrid delivery models.   

Technical fluency with data analysis, SQL, Python, cloud-based data pipelines, CI/CD, or software test automation.   

Experience working with independent assessors,   standards   bodies, regulators, industry consortia, or external technical partners.

jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Role Overview   

 As a Software Engineer in Simulation, you will be responsible for ensuring the quality and reliability of autonomous vehicle simulation platforms. The role bridges hands-on coding, protocol/process definition, integration of metrics, and automated regression monitoring — all foundational to verifying the performance, fidelity, and validity of highly complex simulation systems. This position will follow both collaborative and technical standards with an emphasis on scalable, maintainable, and programmatic approaches.   

About the organization   

 The GM Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) team develops and delivers intelligent, safety, and convenience features to elevate every driver’s experience. By integrating state-of-the-art sensing, perception , and control technologies, GM ADAS empowers vehicles with cutting-edge capabilities . Our cross-functional experts collaborate to design scalable, reliable systems that set new standards for automotive innovation and make mobility easier, safer and more convenient for all.   

The Sim Validation team at GM e nsure s our simulation environments accurately mirror real-world driving conditions and sensor interactions. O n the one hand, b y measuring and monitoring t he realism, accuracy, and coverage of our virtual environments and sensor models, Sim Validation enables developers and engineers to validate autonomous and ADAS technologies with greater realism and confidence .  On the other hand, our validation methodologies establish a basis of trust in our simulation results and capabilities when reporting to executives and regulator y bodies .   Our solutions reduce reliance on physical testing, streamline development, and provide essential insights that guide safer, more robust vehicle systems.   

What you and your team will be doing   

 Build and maintain simulation fidelity and validity metrics, quantifying the gap between simulation and road in novel ways . Construct mechanisms to attribut e issues to components of s imulation systems.   

Design and maintain robust data ingestion and loading tools to support diverse simulation pipelines   

Develop and optimize nodes in both C++ and Python to extract and aggregate metric outputs at scale .     

Create , maintain , and monitor test suites, enabling automated regression detection . Debug, track, and report on validity measures , including deep root-cause analysis . T riage and aid in the prioritization of resolving validation issues.   

Contribute documentation in the form of technical designs , experiment results and internal publications .   

Conduct code reviews and assist teammates in tracking evolving requirements and user workflows .   

Interface with cross-org partners to articulate requirements, resolve handoff issues, and share best practices.   

Required Skills & Qualifications   

 3+ years of experience writing Python in a production environment (unit testing, code review, algorithm performance and tradeoffs, etc.). Demonstrated experience with C++.   

Familiarity with data analysis, e.g. statistics   

Familiarity with SQL, ROS, numpy & scipy , and plotting/visualization libraries   

Excellent communication skills and ability to work independently, driving technical advances.   

BS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Aerospace Engineering or similar experience.   

Bonus points   

 Experience building algorithms central to data analysis of engineering domains    

Experience developing software solutions that are used across engineering teams   

Experience with computational geometry, linear algebra, or Machine Learning   

Experience with time-series data analysis and online performance monitoring tools   

E xperience in simulation/test engineering or automotive autonomy platforms   

Experience automating pipelines, maintaining and troubleshooting test protocols .   

Familiarity with some of Google Cloud, BigQuery , containerized builds, large-scale continuous integration/ monitoring or Python / C++ interoperability

jobs.title: Autonomous Vehicle Test Engineer
jobs.location: Milford, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Position summary 
 GM Level: 6A 

 Proposed job-family alignment: Test and Validation Engineering 

 Primary work location: GM Milford Proving Ground, Milford, Michigan 

 Travel: Approximately 10% as needed for training, team alignment, vehicle support, or other GM testing activities 

 Career track: Individual contributor 

General Motors is developing advanced driving-assistance and autonomous-vehicle capabilities that require safe, repeatable, and scalable validation. The Autonomous Vehicle Test Engineer will plan, execute, and report autonomous-vehicle testing at GM’s Milford Proving Ground in partnership with AV Test Engineering, Vehicle Integration, software and systems engineering, AV Operations, Fleet Reliability Engineering, and other cross-functional teams. 
 
 This role will translate engineering objectives and approved test requests into clear, executable test plans and procedures. The engineer will conduct closed-course regression, feature, behavior, calibration, system-validation, and structured data-collection testing; evaluate vehicle and autonomy-system behavior; troubleshoot software and hardware issues; and deliver complete, actionable evidence to engineering customers. 
 
 The role combines test planning, hands-on vehicle and test execution, technical triage, data analysis, and process improvement. The successful candidate will be comfortable working in a fast-changing environment, taking ownership of ambiguous problems, collaborating across software and hardware domains, and maintaining a high bar for safety, test quality, and technical rigor. 
 
 What you’ll do 
 Plan and execute autonomous-vehicle testing 
 Translate product, software, systems, and program objectives into practical test plans, test cases, procedures, schedules, and resource requirements. 

 Plan and execute repeatable software regression, feature and behavior validation, structured scenario, calibration-support, fault-response, and targeted data-collection tests. 

 Conduct closed-course vehicle testing at Milford Proving Ground, including vehicle preparation, test setup, scenario execution, observation, intervention or takeover when required, and post-run closeout. 

 Coordinate test requests, priorities, vehicle assignments, track reservations, operating windows, personnel, equipment, and readiness reviews with AV Test Engineering and cross-functional stakeholders. 

 Follow approved test procedures and acceptance criteria while using sound engineering judgment when test conditions, vehicle state, system behavior, or data quality differs from expectations. 

 Make timely recommendations to proceed, modify, repeat, block, or stop testing based on safety, vehicle condition, system behavior, track conditions, weather, data quality, or test intent. 

 Support test execution across development and release milestones, including build checkout, regression campaigns, feature validation, system integration, and structured validation activities. 

 Support approved vehicle testing on public roads or other test environments when required by the program, applicable procedures, and GM driver-training and safety requirements. 

 Perform vehicle and system technical triage 
 Monitor vehicle and autonomy-system health before, during, and after testing, identifying conditions that could affect safety, data quality, or test availability. 

 Triage issues involving the AV software stack, vehicle compute, sensors, localization, calibration, connectivity, data recording, host-vehicle systems, vehicle networks, power, and test infrastructure. 

 Use system status, logs, drive data, diagnostic tools, measurements, operator observations, and repeatable experiments to isolate likely causes and determine the appropriate next action. 

 Reproduce issues when safe and practical, capture accurate timelines and evidence, and create actionable issue reports for software, systems, Vehicle Integration, Fleet Reliability Engineering, Troubleforce, Service Operations, or other support teams. 

 Distinguish between issues that can be safely contained or corrected during test execution and issues requiring vehicle removal from service, engineering review, formal change control, or additional safety assessment. 

 Partner with developers and systems engineers to clarify expected behavior, reproduce failures, evaluate fixes, and verify corrective actions through targeted retesting. 

 Support controlled fault-injection and non-nominal testing when requested, ensuring that test intent, expected system response, safety controls, and data-labeling requirements are understood before execution. 

 Deliver high-quality test results and data 
 Execute test procedures consistently and capture complete run information, including vehicle, software, calibration, map, track, scenario, operator, weather, and timing details. 

 Evaluate AV behavior and system response against defined test objectives and acceptance criteria, distinguishing objective evidence from anecdotal observations. 

 Report pass, fail, blocked, incomplete, and inconclusive outcomes with enough context for engineering teams to act without repeating avoidable setup work. 

 Ensure drive links, logs, data media, notes, screenshots, issue references, and other required evidence are transferred or uploaded through approved workflows. 

 Review test data for completeness, corruption, missing signals, unexpected configuration changes, or other conditions that could limit its usefulness. 

 Publish concise test summaries, technical findings, and status updates to the appropriate engineering and operations forums. 

 Maintain traceability for test requests, procedures, results, issues, and retests in tools such as Jira, Confluence, Xray, Slack, and approved data or fleet-management systems. 

 Provide timely feedback to remote software, systems, simulation, safety, and program teams so that test results support release decisions, feature refinement, and issue prioritization. 

 Support vehicle readiness and test execution infrastructure 
 Prepare assigned test vehicles and equipment for daily execution, including configuration checks, software and calibration state, physical condition, instrumentation, data-recording readiness, and required test assets. 

 Perform or coordinate pre-drive readiness checks, post-drive inspections, sensor and camera cleanliness checks, data-media handling, charging or fueling coordination, and other activities required to maintain test availability. 

 Support approved software or branch deployments, calibration updates, route or map selection, logging configuration, test tools, and other test-preparation activities. 

 Maintain accurate records of vehicle status, mileage or test hours, configuration, test history, open issues, and return-to-service decisions. 

 Identify vehicle downtime risks early and coordinate containment, recovery, maintenance, parts, facility resources, and technical assistance with the appropriate partner teams. 

 Help maintain reliable test infrastructure, track resources, measurement equipment, data workflows, and other assets needed for repeatable execution. 

 Contribute to readiness reviews and daily operating rhythms that align vehicle and facility availability with testing demand. 

 Collaborate across the AV development lifecycle 
 Work closely with AV Test Engineering leads, Vehicle Integration, software engineering, systems engineering, AV Operations, Fleet Reliability Engineering, Service Operations, Safety, Mapping, Simulation, and program teams. 

 Clarify test objectives, assumptions, expected system behavior, inputs, outputs, dependencies, and acceptance criteria before execution. 

 Coordinate with operations personnel and technicians to ensure vehicles, track activities, equipment, and supporting tasks are prepared and executed safely. 

 Provide clear technical direction during test execution when coordinating operators, technicians, contractors, or other support personnel, without formal people-management responsibility. 

 Communicate blockers, risks, schedule impacts, vehicle constraints, and issue status early enough for teams to make informed decisions. 

 Participate in technical reviews, release-readiness discussions, issue reviews, retrospectives, and other forums that improve test effectiveness and system quality. 

 Build trusted working relationships across disciplines by being responsive, precise, fact-based, and accountable for follow-through. 

 Improve test methods, tools, and operating processes 
 Identify opportunities to increase usable testing hours, improve coverage, reduce avoidable setup and reset time, and improve the quality and timeliness of test results. 

 Develop and maintain clear checklists, test templates, troubleshooting guides, readiness gates, standard work, and other documentation that improves repeatability. 

 Improve test intake, prioritization, planning, execution, reporting, issue follow-up, and data-management workflows. 

 Use metrics and evidence such as vehicle availability, test hours, completed runs, blocked runs, downtime, repeat failures, data-upload timeliness, issue aging, and request cycle time to identify improvement opportunities. 

 Support appropriate automation, tooling, and data-analysis improvements that reduce manual effort and increase test consistency. 

 Capture lessons learned from test campaigns and convert them into improved test plans, procedures, asset requirements, and recommendations. 

 Help onboard and share knowledge with other engineers, technicians, operators, and cross-functional partners. 

 Maintain a Safety First culture 
 Follow all GM, Milford Proving Ground, AV Operations, AV Test Engineering, and applicable safety procedures and work controls. 

 Verify that required personnel, training, vehicle qualifications, test equipment, track conditions, emergency support, communications, and approved procedures are in place before testing begins. 

 Stop work and escalate when vehicle condition, system behavior, weather, track conditions, personnel readiness, facility conditions, or test setup creates unacceptable risk. 

 Maintain disciplined adherence to approved operating limits, test procedures, takeover requirements, driver guidance, and change-control expectations. 

 Support incident, near-miss, and abnormal-event documentation with accurate facts, timelines, evidence, and follow-up actions. 

 Treat safety, data integrity, and test traceability as non-negotiable requirements for every test activity. 

 Required qualifications 
 Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, automotive, systems, computer, robotics, aerospace engineering, computer science, or a related technical discipline. 

 At least 3 years of relevant experience in autonomous vehicles, automotive engineering, robotics, aerospace, vehicle testing, systems integration, test engineering, or a related technical operations environment. 

 Experience planning and executing vehicle, robotics, or other complex electro-mechanical system tests in a laboratory, proving-ground, field, or comparable operational environment. 

 Experience troubleshooting software-enabled hardware systems using diagnostic information, logs, measurements, observations, and structured problem-solving methods. 

 Ability to read and apply test procedures, requirements, acceptance criteria, operating instructions, and safety controls. 

 Demonstrated ability to take ownership, establish priorities, work independently, and drive ambiguous technical problems toward resolution. 

 Ability to collaborate effectively with software, hardware, systems, operations, reliability, safety, and program teams. 

 Strong written and verbal communication skills, including concise technical reporting, issue escalation, and cross-functional coordination. 

 Ability to work onsite in a proving-ground environment with exposure to heat, cold, dust, wind, sun, noise, vehicle traffic, and changing work conditions. 

 Ability to perform hands-on vehicle readiness and troubleshooting activities, including inspecting vehicles, connecting or handling test equipment and data media, and moving through vehicle and track environments as required. 

 Ability to work onsite at GM Milford Proving Ground in Milford, Michigan, and travel approximately 10% as needed. 

 Valid driver’s license and ability to meet applicable GM driver-training, vehicle-qualification, site-access, and safety requirements for vehicle testing. 

 Preferred qualifications 
 Direct experience testing autonomous vehicles, advanced driver-assistance systems, mobile robots, or other safety-critical autonomous systems. 

 Experience with closed-course test execution, proving-ground operations, scripted scenario testing, release regression, feature validation, calibration support, or structured data collection. 

 Experience with total-vehicle integration, vehicle systems testing, or end-to-end validation of software-enabled vehicle features. 

 Working knowledge of software-defined vehicle concepts, SDV 2.0 architecture, vehicle compute, electronic control units, over-the-air or branch-based software deployment, vehicle configuration, and software or hardware change management. 

 Experience with automotive diagnostics, CAN or Ethernet-based vehicle networks, sensors, localization, calibration, time synchronization, data recording, connectivity, or AV system-health monitoring. 

 Familiarity with AV and vehicle tools such as Xray, INCA, Vehicle Spy, DPS, Cursor, Git, GitHub, Buildkite, Grafana, Notelogger, SC3 Debug App, Jumpstart, Launchpad, Starfleet, HAT, Drives, Webviz, Netradyne, Looker, or comparable tools. 

 Experience using Linux, command-line tools, Python, SQL, spreadsheets, or other methods to inspect logs, automate repetitive analysis, or improve test and fleet reporting. 

 Experience with test-management, issue-tracking, configuration-management, or release tools such as Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Artifactory, or comparable platforms. 

 Familiarity with software development life-cycle practices, integration workflows, requirements traceability, and release-readiness processes. 

 Experience working with AV, automotive, robotics, or other complex systems in a fast-paced development environment. 

 Experience supporting or mentoring technicians, operators, junior engineers, contractors, or other test-support personnel.

The compensation may not be representative for positions located outside of New York, Colorado, California, or Washington.

 Ensure drive links, logs, hard drives or data media, notes, screenshots, issue references, and other required evidence are transferred or uploaded through approved workflows.

 Review test data for completeness, corruption, missing signals, unexpected configuration changes, or other conditions that could limit its usefulness.

 Publish concise test summaries and status updates to the appropriate engineering and operations forums, and maintain traceability in tools such as Jira, Confluence, Xray, Slack, and approved data or fleet-management systems.

 Provide timely feedback to remote software, systems, simulation, safety, and program teams so that test results support release decisions, feature refinement, and issue prioritization.

 Establish a dependable Yuma operating model
 Help stand up and continuously improve the permanent Yuma closed-course testing capability, including roles, standard work, readiness gates, communications, operating rhythms, and handoffs with the broader AV Test Engineering and AV Operations organizations.

 Maintain a repeatable intake-to-execution workflow for local test requests, including request clarification, prioritization, planning, execution, results reporting, and issue follow-up.

 Create and maintain onsite documentation for vehicle checkout, test preparation, track use, safety controls, data handling, troubleshooting, emergency response, and end-of-day closeout.

 Coordinate with DPG Site Operations, Safety, Infrastructure, Mapping, security, and other facility partners to ensure the local operation meets site requirements and has the resources needed to execute safely.

 Track local performance indicators such as vehicle availability, test hours, completed runs, blocked runs, downtime, repeat failures, data-upload timeliness, issue aging, and test-request cycle time.

 Identify opportunities to increase usable testing hours, reduce avoidable setup and reset time, improve vehicle utilization, and shift repeatable work to appropriately trained operations personnel.

 Capture lessons learned from winter testing and other campaigns and convert them into improved test plans, asset requirements, procedures, and recommendations for future scaling.

 Maintain a Safety First culture
 Follow all GM, DPG, AV Operations, AV Test Engineering, and applicable safety procedures and work controls.

 Verify that required personnel, training, vehicle qualifications, test equipment, track conditions, emergency support, communications, and approved procedures are in place before testing begins.

 Stop work and escalate when vehicle condition, system behavior, weather, track conditions, personnel readiness, facility conditions, or test setup creates unacceptable risk.

 Maintain the requirement that testing is conducted with appropriate onsite personnel and never rely on unsupported lone-person operations or unapproved after-hours activity.

 Support incident, near-miss, and abnormal-event documentation with accurate facts, timelines, evidence, and follow-up actions.

 Required qualifications
 Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, automotive, systems, computer, robotics, aerospace engineering, computer science, or a related technical discipline.

 At least 3 years of relevant experience in autonomous vehicles, automotive engineering, robotics, aerospace, vehicle testing, systems integration, test engineering, or a related technical operations environment.

 Experience planning and executing vehicle, robotics, or other complex electro-mechanical system tests in a laboratory, proving-ground, field, or comparable operational environment.

 Experience troubleshooting software-enabled hardware systems using diagnostic information, logs, measurements, observations, and structured problem-solving methods.

 Ability to read and apply test procedures, requirements, acceptance criteria, operating instructions, and safety controls.

 Demonstrated ability to work independently, establish priorities, take initiative, and maintain ownership in an environment with limited onsite support.

 Ability to provide clear technical direction to operators, coordinators, contractors, or other support personnel during test execution without formal people-management responsibility.

 Strong written and verbal communication skills, including concise technical reporting, issue escalation, and remote collaboration across time zones and functions.

 Ability to work outdoors and in a proving-ground environment with exposure to heat, cold, dust, wind, sun, noise, vehicle traffic, and changing work conditions.

 Ability to perform hands-on vehicle readiness and troubleshooting activities, including inspecting vehicles, connecting or handling test equipment and data media, and moving through vehicle and track environments as required.

 Ability to work onsite at GM Desert Proving Ground in Yuma, Arizona, and travel approximately 10% as needed.

 Valid driver’s license and ability to meet applicable GM driver-training, vehicle-qualification, site-access, and safety requirements for closed-course vehicle testing.

 Preferred qualifications
 Direct experience testing autonomous vehicles, advanced driver-assistance systems, mobile robots, or other safety-critical autonomous systems.

 Experience with closed-course test execution, proving-ground operations, scripted scenario testing, release regression, feature validation, calibration support, or structured data collection.

 Experience owning a small test fleet or vehicle asset set, including vehicle readiness, configuration management, downtime recovery, maintenance coordination, and return-to-service decisions.

 Working knowledge of software-defined vehicle concepts, SDV 2.0 architecture, vehicle compute, electronic control units, over-the-air or branch-based software deployment, vehicle configuration, and software/hardware change management.

 Experience with automotive diagnostics, CAN or Ethernet-based vehicle networks, sensors, localization, calibration, time synchronization, data recording, connectivity, or AV system health monitoring.

 Familiarity with AV and vehicle tools such as Xray, INCA, Vehicle Spy, Notelogger, SC3 Debug App, Jumpstart, Launchpad, Starfleet, HAT, Drives, Webviz, Netradyne, Grafana, Looker, or comparable tools.

 Experience using Linux, command-line tools, Python, SQL, spreadsheets, or other methods to inspect logs, automate repetitive analysis, or improve test and fleet reporting.

 Experience directing small operational teams or contractors in a safety-critical, field, laboratory, proving-ground, or shift-based environment.

 Experience working at GM Desert Proving Ground, Yuma Proving Ground, Milford Proving Ground, or another proving ground with limited onsite technical support.

 Familiarity with formal issue-management, root-cause, change-control, safety-case, or corrective-action processes.

 Experience testing in variable weather, winter conditions, desert conditions, or other environments where facility and vehicle readiness directly affect test capacity.

jobs.title: Staff ML Engineer - Embodied AI Onboard Autonomy
jobs.location: Sunnyvale, California, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Are you passionate about accelerating the future of autonomous driving? Join the Embodied AI team at General Motors. Our team is developing and deploying machine learning solutions that support safe and reliable autonomous vehicle behavior across real-world scenarios.
 
 As a Staff AI/ML Engineer within the Onboard Embodied AI organization, you will be a senior individual contributor driving cutting-edge end-to-end machine learning solutions directly impacting autonomous driving performance. Your role is pivotal in designing, architecting, and deploying advanced ML models that translate raw sensor data into actionable driving behaviors, enabling vehicles to robustly navigate diverse real-world scenarios and conditions. You'll lead critical technical initiatives, collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, mentor ML engineers, and significantly shape the future of onboard ML capabilities. 
 
 The Onboard Embodied AI team is at the forefront of developing groundbreaking onboard ML systems powering fully autonomous vehicles. We leverage modern end-to-end machine learning approaches with sophisticated neural networks trained from large-scale driving data and using state-of-the-art alignment approaches. Our solutions enable vehicles to understand complex, dynamic driving environments, handle uncertainty gracefully, and adapt seamlessly to changing conditions. Join a collaborative and innovative team redefining autonomy through state-of-the-art machine learning, delivering solutions that move beyond current technological boundaries. 
 
 Key Responsibilities:   
 Drive the design, development, and deployment of advanced onboard ML models, delivering end-to-end solutions capable of real-time inference and robust autonomous driving performance.  

 Lead and architect complex machine learning projects, from conception through validation to onboard implementation, emphasizing scalability, robustness, and safety-critical operation.  

 Champion innovation in neural network architectures, training methodologies, and inference optimization strategies suited for real-time onboard deployment.  

 Provide technical mentorship and thought leadership, elevating engineering practices, and fostering ML innovation across teams.  

 Collaborate closely with multidisciplinary engineering groups, ensuring seamless integration of ML capabilities into autonomous vehicle systems.  

 Influence technical roadmaps, shaping strategic ML priorities aligned with company objectives and product milestones.  

Your Skills & Abilities:   
 Master's or Ph.D. in Machine Learning, Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.  

 4+ years of experience working with large-scale Foundation Models, including LLMs, VLAs and vision-focused models. 

 Extensive experience developing and deploying advanced ML systems, particularly in end-to-end real-time onboard applications.  

 Proven track record as a technical expert in developing robust deep learning models that directly map sensor data to actionable outputs within safety-critical systems.  

 Deep expertise in state-of-the-art computer vision techniques, neural architectures, representation learning, real-time inference, model optimization, and robustness under uncertainty.   

 Strong software engineering proficiency, particularly Python and C++, alongside extensive hands-on experience with modern ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX).  

 Excellent communication, collaboration, and mentoring abilities, comfortable influencing technical strategy and guiding ML engineering excellence across the organization. 

 AV/ADAS experience is a big plus

jobs.description:
Job Description 
 This is a 2nd shift opportunity
 This job may be eligible for relocation benefits
 
 GM DOES NOT PROVIDE IMMIGRATION-RELATED SPONSORSHIP FOR THIS ROLE. DO NOT APPLY FOR THIS ROLE IF YOU WILL NEED GM IMMIGRATION SPONSORSHIP (e.g., H-1B, TN, STEM OPT, etc.) NOW OR IN THE FUTURE.
 
 Onsite: This role is categorized as onsite. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Orion, MI on a full-time basis.
 The Role 
 The Senior Controls Engineer- Body Shop is responsible for providing advanced controls engineering leadership and technical oversight within a highly automated automotive body shop environment. This role serves as a key technical expert supporting robotic welding, material handling, joining technologies, and automated production systems . The position requires a high degree of independent judgment and technical authority to achieve safety, quality, cost, throughput, and launch objectives while ensuring the long-term reliability and maintainability of body shop equipment and controls systems.
 
 What You'll Do 
 Lead controls engineering strategy and execution for body shop manufacturing systems
 Serve as the technical authority for PLC, robotics, and network architecture standards.
 Manage and execute complex electrical and controls projects including new installations, major upgrades, model change activities, throughput improvements, and lifecycle replacements.
 Develop and approve cost estimates, investment forecasts, business cases, and appropriation requests for capital projects.
 Provide technical mentorship to Controls Engineers, Automation Engineers, and Skilled Trades across multiple shifts.
 Lead root cause analysis and resolution of complex equipment and system failures.
 Drive continuous improvement initiatives utilizing statistical methods and data-driven decision making.
 Coordinate with Manufacturing Engineering, corporate engineering organizations, and suppliers on new model planning, CQPI, sourcing, and equipment validation.
 Establish and manage project support plans between plant operations, corporate engineering, and contractor resources.
 Represent Engineering in plant leadership meetings and cross-functional business planning activities.
 Influence plant-wide goals through Business Plan Deployment and cross-functional alignment.
 Support implementation of Global Manufacturing Systems and Quality Network initiatives to improve operational excellence.
 Oversee development and adherence to engineering standards, documentation, and best practices.
 Develop and monitor project schedules, risk mitigation plans, and execution timelines.
 Provide input into plant capital planning and Central Manufacturing Engineering budgets.
 Ensure long-term reliability, maintainability, and cost efficiency of manufacturing equipment and infrastructure.
 Drive energy efficiency, operational cost reduction, and maximum throughput strategies.
 Partner with Plant Training teams to develop and deploy training for new technologies introduced to the facility.
 Champion safety as the highest priority, enforcing safe work practices and driving improvements in ergonomics, health, safety, and housekeeping.
 Maintain strong working relationships with hourly employees, union leadership, plant management, suppliers, and external support organizations.
 
 Your Skills and Abilities (Required Qualifications) 
 Advanced ability to program, troubleshoot, and optimize Rockwell/Allen-Bradley ControlLogix PLC systems in high-volume automotive manufacturing environments.
 Advanced troubleshooting and programming experience with FANUC robotic systems, including robot path recovery, fault diagnostics, and production optimization. 
 Strong understanding of welding systems, weld controllers, weld schedules, and robotic welding applications? 
 Expert ability to read, interpret, and modify electrical schematic and controls documentation.
 Advanced troubleshooting experience with automated body shop manufacturing systems, material handling equipment, and conveyor controls. 
 Strong knowledge of industrial communication networks including Ethernet/IP, DeviceNet, ControlNet, and integrated robot-to-PLC communication. 
 Experience supporting safety-rated control systems, robot safety zones, interlocks, and machine safeguarding requirements.
 Strong analytical and structured problem-solving capabilities utilizing root cause analysis and data-driven methodologies.
 Effective leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills with the ability to influence cross-functional teams.
 Willingness to work 2nd shift
 Willingness to support weekend or extended hours during critical production and project phases.
 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Five or more years of experience in automotive body shop, welding, or assembly manufacturing operations. 
 Experience supporting robotic welding cells, framing systems, underbody/body-side lines, or final body assembly processes. 
 Experience leading automation strategies, major equipment installations, or large capital projects in a body shop environment.
 Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, or equivalent technical experience.
 Experience with manufacturing systems integration including (MES, SCADA, data acquisition)
 Knowledge of dimensional quality systems, automated measurement technologies, and body build quality requirements. 
 Demonstrated experience leading, mentoring, or supervising engineering and technical teams.
 Experience supporting new vehicle launches, tooling integration, and production ramp-up activities

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Autonomy Evaluation
jobs.location: Remote - United States
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 General Motors is a global leader in advanced driver   assistance . With   Super Cruise   hands-free technology in more than 500,000 Super Cruise–equipped vehicles on the road and over 700 million hands-free miles driven, GM is proving that automation can be trusted, intuitive, and helpful. GM has the global reach to bring   cutting-edge   advances to everyday drivers at   unprecedented   scale. Join us to help deliver the next generation of safe and delightful personal autonomous vehicle experiences.   

About the Organization    

 The   Evaluation team   builds and evolves the evaluation ecosystem that powers the development and scaling of GM’s autonomous driving technology. We develop metrics, automated workflows, and analysis approaches that enable data-driven decisions across AV development and verification. Partnering with Autonomy, Simulation, Systems, and Safety teams, we act as system-level integrators and arbiters of end-to-end AV quality.   

 We own large-scale test scenario libraries, continuous evaluation pipelines, and critical risk assessment and release-gating components, treating road testing, data mining, training, and metrics as first-class use cases in a unified analytics framework. By joining this team, you will help shape GM’s core evaluation platforms, turn system-level results into clear feedback for engineering and leadership, and help accelerate validated AV deployment at scale.   

What   You’ll   Do (Responsibilities)   

 Architect and implement metrics and analyses to introspect autonomous driving software performance at   interfaces across the autonomy stack; partner closely with autonomy developers and systems engineers.   

Design and implement analysis algorithms that summarize, aggregate, and cluster metrics produced by simulations and on-road runs of the autonomy stack.   

Propose and develop new statistical and ML methods to quantify performance and   identify   patterns of system and subsystem behavior across diverse scenes and operational domains.   

Develop and apply methods to introspect the operation of ML components in the autonomy stack, including evaluation of   perception , prediction, and planning models.   

Build and   maintain   autonomy   evaluation   dashboards and interactive reports that provide clear, explainable insights (e.g., trend analysis, drift detection, scenario coverage) for development, verification, and leadership.   

Leverage vision-language models (VLMs) and large language models (LLMs), where   appropriate , to classify autonomy performance,   identify   critical scenarios, and prioritize validation efforts, integrating human-in-the-loop review where needed.   

Maintain a high technical standard through thoughtful system design, code reviews, testing, observability, and adherence to software-engineering best practices.   

Interface with cross-organizational partners to articulate requirements, resolve handoff issues, and share best practices around evaluation, metrics, and experiment design.   

Your Skills & Abilities   (Required Qualifications)   

 5+ years of applied experience with robotics or autonomous systems software (e.g., sensors,   perception , prediction, planning, or control), data analysis, ML evaluation, or autonomy analytics.   

3+ years evaluating dynamic systems using numerical and/or ML approaches, including time-series data, state derivatives, dynamics, and interconnected subsystems.   

Strong   proficiency   developing   Python   in production team environments, including testing, performance, and code review.   

Proficiency   with   Pandas, NumPy, SciPy ,   and plotting/visualization libraries for large-scale data analysis and reporting.   

Comfort working with   C++   codebases, including reading, debugging, and instrumenting core algorithms.   

A strong curiosity to question anomalous data and systematically root-cause discrepancies.   

Demonstrated technical leadership, including driving architectural decisions, influencing cross-team designs, and owning complex features or services end-to-end.   

Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in   C omputer Science, Robotics, Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering, Machine Learning, Data Science , or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.   

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)   

 Experience in   a utonomous driving or field robotics , including visualizing and interpreting results from simulation and field experiments.   

Experience evaluating robotics or AV systems using   sensor data   (e.g., camera, lidar, radar) and large-scale   time-series   analysis.   

Strong intuition for   data visualization   and the ability to decompose high-dimensional metrics into clear, trustworthy, and consumable views for technical and non-technical audiences.   

Familiarity with   statistical modeling, experimental design, and hypothesis   testing   for autonomy or simulation evaluation; fluency with Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, and visualization tools.   

Proficiency   in   C++ and SQL ; experience shaping logging, data schemas, and evaluation pipelines for large-scale autonomy testing and performance monitoring.   

Experience working with   ROS or similar robotics/IPC frameworks , log pipelines, and large-scale experiment databases or evaluation platforms.   

Prior development experience with   computational geometry, linear algebra,   PyTorch , and ML techniques applied to   perception , prediction, planning, or control.   

Background in modeling   agent interaction   and contributing to   release gating   and safety decisions for autonomy systems.   

Experience   leveraging   AI-assisted development and analytics tools   to improve productivity and evaluation coverage.

jobs.location: Milford, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 DUTIES: Generate technical solutions including specifying of requirements, functional decomposition, analysis, development and testing for current, new and major programs. Perform as Subject Matter Expert (SME) for at least one platform or application component and participates in interviews. Verify controller functionality on a bench and vehicle. Work with Technical Review Boards and other cross functional teams to define test cases and to determine how frequently they should be executed. Automate system level test cases to allow for automated regression testing. Troubleshoot vehicle level integration issues including hardware, software, calibration and vehicle wiring. Document hardware and software anomalies using Rational Team Concert (RTC) or similar database. Confirm resolution of documented hardware and software anomalies. Support algorithm requirement development by supporting algorithm technical review boards. Document algorithm functional and verification requirements. Develop, document, and review I/O functional requirements and test cases. Conduct and participate in work product reviews for algorithm, software, and specifications incorporating I/O functional requirements and test cases. Provide support as required: Software support for calibration teams and development trips, assembly plant and field problem resolution, prototype shop support, and durability cars and captured test fleet support. Hybrid Work Policy - 3 days In-office, 2 days remote - Must be able to report to local office.

REQUIREMENTS: Master's degree in Electronic Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field of study and Four (4) years of experience as a Software Engineer, Programmer Analyst, Development Engineer, Release Engineer or related role. Three (3) years of experience with: Embedded systems, including their architecture and components in automotive applications including control systems, sensor integration, and real-time processing; Using diagnostic tools like Vector CANoe, CANalyzer, and VehicleSpy for signal monitoring, and fault isolation; Interpreting software logs and error codes to identify root causes in code and system behavior; Automotive communication protocols including CAN, LIN, FlexRay, and Ethernet to trace data flows and understand network behaviors; Interpreting test data, identify patterns in failures, and apply structured problem-solving approaches; Root cause analysis including 5 Whys and Fishbone Diagram, and failure mode analysis; Vehicle electrical systems and mechanical components for diagnosing mechatronic issues where hardware and software intersect; Systems engineering principles to see how
 individual components, including hardware, software, and calibrations, interact within the larger vehicle system; Analyzing requirements to ensure each component and system function meets design intent and customer expectations; Calibration management, with ETAS INCA and Vector CANape, to modify and validate parameter settings in real time; Diagnosing hardware-related issues, from PCB-level component failure to wiring harness issues, grounding problems, and sensor malfunctions; Using multimeters, oscilloscopes, and other electrical diagnostic tools to validate hardware functionality; and ECU reprogramming tools and protocols including UDS to handle in-field updates and support assembly plant staff in flashing procedures. One (1) year of experience with: Lauterbach and GreenHills Multi for data capture, hardware and software debugging; Software development tools including Git, Gerrit, Jenkins, and IDEs including Eclipse; and Software flashing techniques, including Over-the-Air (OTA) updates, to support vehicle software updates and troubleshoot any issues that arise during flashing.

 As a   Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) Engineer   within General Motors’   A V Core Infrastructure team , you will design, build, and   maintain   advanced HIL systems that accelerate validation of embedded controllers and   perception   systems across next- generation   vehicles.   You’ll   bridge mechanical, electrical, and software disciplines to deliver scalable, reliable, and maintainable test infrastructure enabling data-driven development   of automated driving features.   

 You will collaborate with systems engineers, embedded software developers, integration labs, and operations teams to ensure our HIL platforms   remain   at the forefront of validation capability—powering the test flywheel that drives GM’s future of safe, autonomous mobility.

 Design, build, and sustain   modular HIL systems for ECU and subsystem validation across multiple vehicle platforms.   

De velop   scalable rack-based test solutions   integrating power distribution, network infrastructure, and environmental management for high-availability   operations .   

Collaborate cross-functionally   with Systems, Firmware, and Validation Engineering to define I/O mappings, harnessing, and test configurations.   

Deploy automation and monitoring systems   for bench health, including power cycling, network diagnostics, and logging infrastructure.   

Drive lab capacity expansion projects , including facility layout, power/network planning, and thermal management.   

Continuously   innovate   to improve efficiency, reusability, and modularity across the HIL fleet; contribute to design libraries and shared tools.   

Complete   bench   bring up, parts ordering, and integration of components ranging from boards to   sensors .     

Support flashing and configuration changes and develop preventative maintenance   processes   to ensure bench fleet health.

Required Qualifications   

 Bachelor's degree in mechanical , Electrical, or Mechatronics Engineering—or equivalent hands-on experience in HIL, lab automation, or robotics integration.   

4 + years of experience in design, integration, and maintenance of hardware validation systems or HIL infrastructure.   

Familiarity with   ECU harnessing, power systems, and signal integrity best practices .   

Competence with   Linux CLI, networking (Ethernet, switches, VLANs), and power distribution .   

Proven record of   cross-functional collaboration , vendor management, and hands-on debugging of complex electromechanical systems.
